logline: An idealist rookie judge and a pragmatic senior judge navigate a Seoul courtroom where human disputes - petty and profound - reveal the cracks in both law and society.

renewal.note: 16-episode limited series, completed July 2018. Based on the serialised novel by Seoul Eastern District Court chief judge Moon Yoo-seok. No continuation planned.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb rates it 7.4/10. Critics praised its insider authenticity - written by an actual sitting judge - and its honest depiction of modern Korean social tensions. Reviewer consensus places it at a solid 7.5, with praise for character work over plot mechanics.

pull_quotes.text: Miss Hammurabi defied the odds and kept me interested all the way through. It gave me fantastic characters and a great script.

seasons.review_body: Ms. Hammurabi aired on JTBC from May to July 2018, with a unique claim to authenticity: its screenplay was based on a novel written by Moon Yoo-seok, a serving chief judge at the Seoul Eastern District Court. That inside view shows. The show was praised by viewers and critics for its fresh, non-glamourised portrait of Korean judges - the administrative grind, the moral compromises, the cases that resist clean resolution. Lead performances by Go Ara and Kim Myung-soo drew appreciation for their chemistry and contrasting judicial philosophies. The IMDb rating of 7.4 reflects an audience that found the episodic case structure occasionally unfocused but the character writing consistently strong. For viewers who find Korean legal drama too courtroom-procedural, this slice-of-life approach functions as a meaningful corrective.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A confident opening that establishes the show's register - less about legal verdicts, more about the people who give and receive them. The rookie-meets-veteran dynamic is drawn with more nuance than the genre usually allows.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first case seen through the idealist judge's eyes sets up the series' central tension between what justice looks like on paper and what it feels like in practice.
